You are working against a live production Kubernetes cluster: GKE cluster
"gitops-pilot-20260916-132249" in project "fuxiaogao-gkedemos".

Checkout has been stuck at only part of its usual instance count since this morning's build update, and on-call is on it now. New instances keep failing to start. Please investigate and remediate.

The cluster's desired state is tracked in the git repository
https://github.com/gke-agentic/fuxiao-gkedemo-infra under "tasks/b-0011" on branch
"run/gitops-pilot-20260916-132249/b-0011", which Argo CD syncs to this cluster. Changes reach

output:
🔀 Delegated to the cluster-fuxiaogao-gkedemos-gitops-pilot-20260916-13224-b913022f agent

I've started the diagnosis as task t_c4842c10. The RCA and proposed fix will post into this thread; once I have it I'll hand the remediation PR to the platform agent against run/gitops-pilot-20260916-132249/b-0011.

t_c4842c10 — done (completed 2026-09-16, child card t_9a2ee7f4 filed for the remediation PR). Complete result:

## Root cause

This morning's build update raised the `checkout` container memory request **4x, from `64Mi` to `256Mi`**, which pushed the `payments` namespace past its `ResourceQuota` hard cap. New pods are **rejected at admission** — they are never created, never scheduled, never run. This is not a crash, image pull, probe or capacity problem.

Verbatim rejection from `ReplicaSet/checkout-8448b6988`:

`Error creating: pods "checkout-8448b6988-f8rkq" is forbidden: exceeded quota: payments-quota, requested: requests.memory=256Mi, used: requests.memory=832Mi, limited: requests.memory=832Mi`

Deployment `checkout` (uid `0812fb0c-42ce-4f17-9c2a-09b3710a1e75`) carries condition `ReplicaFailure/FailedCreate` since `2026-09-16T17:35:31Z`, at `readyReplicas: 3` of `replicas: 4`.

## Evidence

The rollout is **permanently wedged, not slow**. Quota `payments-quota` hard cap is `requests.memory: 832Mi` (`used: 704Mi`), but the target steady state now needs `4 x 256Mi` (checkout) `+ 2 x 64Mi` (pricer) = **`1152Mi`**, and up to `1408Mi` mid-rollout with `maxSurge: 25%`. It can never converge. Before the bump it needed `4 x 64Mi + 128Mi` = `384Mi`, comfortably inside the cap.

The image change is a **red herring**: `:1.0` and `:1.0.0` resolve to the *same* digest `sha256:fcb75f691c8b0414d670ae570240cbf95502cc18a9ba57e982ecac589760a186`. Both old and new pods pulled fine and are `Ready 1/1` with `0` restarts, so nothing justifies a 4x memory increase.

Not capacity: the single node has `6170284Ki` allocatable and reports **no** `MemoryPressure`. No HPA and no LimitRange exist in `payments`. The three running pods are healthy.

| Revision | Image | Mem request | Ready |
|---|---|---|---|
| `595f7f4d8c` (rev 1) | `:1.0` | `64Mi` | 1 |
| `8448b6988` (rev 2) | `:1.0.0` | `256Mi` | 2 |

## Proposed fix

Revert the request in `tasks/b-0011` on branch `run/gitops-pilot-20260916-132249/b-0011` of [fuxiao-gkedemo-infra](https://github.com/gke-agentic/fuxiao-gkedemo-infra) — `Deployment/checkout`, container `web`:

```yaml
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 64Mi   # was 256Mi — restores 384Mi steady state, inside the 832Mi cap
```

Keeping `256Mi` is viable **only** if paired with raising `payments-quota` `spec.hard.requests.memory` to at least `1408Mi` (covers rollout surge) — that quota is owned by `platform-team` under [CAP-418](https://tickets.acme.internal/CAP-418), so it needs their sign-off. Given the identical image digest, reverting the request is the correct fix.

**Worth remembering:** `payments` is governed by a memory-requests-only `ResourceQuota` (`payments-quota`, owner `platform-team`, ticket CAP-418) sized with no rolling-update surge headroom, so any memory-request increase to a workload in `payments` wedges the rollout unless the quota is raised in the same change.

## Grounding

Cluster [gitops-pilot-20260916-132249](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/clusters/details/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-20260916-132249/details?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) (`us-central1-a`, project `fuxiaogao-gkedemos`), namespace `payments`, workload [checkout](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/deployment/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-20260916-132249/payments/checkout/overview?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos). Read-only: `get deployment/replicaset/pod/resourcequota/limitrange/node/hpa/application`, `list_k8s_events`. Event window `2026-09-16T17:34:56Z`–`17:38:38Z`; Argo CD app `b-0011` synced rev `51e1abbd48422ceb5798ccc368de4412f710ff84` at `17:35:28Z`. No cluster state was mutated. `pods/log` was RBAC-denied for `kubeagents-platform-gsa@fuxiaogao-gkedemos.iam.gserviceaccount.com`; not load-bearing, since the failure is at admission and no container ever starts.

## Sources

- `mcp__gke__*` (read-only GKE MCP) for all live cluster evidence.
- `mcp__developer_knowledge__answer_query` on ResourceQuota enforcement during rolling updates, citing [GKE enterprise multitenancy best practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/best-practices/enterprise-multitenancy) and [cost-effective Kubernetes applications on GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/best-practices-for-running-cost-effective-kubernetes-applications-on-gke).

t_9a2ee7f4 — done (completed 2026-09-16 17:48). Complete result:

PR is open: [gke-agentic/fuxiao-gkedemo-infra#36](https://github.com/gke-agentic/fuxiao-gkedemo-infra/pull/36) — reverts `checkout` memory request `256Mi` → `64Mi`, targeting `run/gitops-pilot-20260916-132249/b-0011`. Nothing was pushed to that branch directly.

## The change

One file, one line: `tasks/b-0011/10-workloads.yaml`, `Deployment/checkout` container `web`, `+1/-1`.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Head branch | `platform-agent/revert-checkout-memory-b-0011-20260916-132249` |
| Base branch | `run/gitops-pilot-20260916-132249/b-0011` |
| Commit | `155fafc9904f` on base `51e1abbd` |

Verified against the live PR: `changedFiles: 1`, and the diff is only `memory: 256Mi` → `memory: 64Mi`. The image tag stays `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0.0` (same digest as `:1.0`), and `ResourceQuota/payments-quota` is untouched — the `1408Mi` alternative is platform-team's under [CAP-418](https://tickets.acme.internal/CAP-418) and only applies if the app genuinely needs `256Mi`, which nothing shows.

The PR body carries the RCA from [card `t_c4842c10`](https://github.com/gke-agentic/fuxiao-gkedemo-infra/pull/36): admission rejection against the `832Mi` hard limit, not a crash loop or OOMKill. After sync, steady state is `4x64Mi` + `2x64Mi` = `384Mi` against `832Mi`, so the fourth replica is admitted and `checkout` returns to `4/4`.

## Follow-up filed

Card `t_92c56e1c` — the `KUBECONFIG` pin. I agreed with the cluster agent and went further: `USER.md` in that profile says the authoritative pin lives in the profile's `.env`, and **no `/opt/data/profiles/cluster-*` profile has a `.env` at all** — all 13, not just this cluster. The kubeconfig files themselves are correct. `cluster_agent_profile.py` cannot run from the shell sandbox (the on-disk copy there is a stand-in stub), so that card may need the agent pod.

**Worth remembering**
- `payments-quota` on `gitops-pilot-*` is memory-requests-only with no rolling-update surge headroom, so any memory-request increase in `payments` wedges the rollout at admission unless the quota moves in the same change.
- `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0` and `:1.0.0` are the same digest, so a build update moving between them is a no-op and cannot justify a resource change.
- Cluster Agent profiles have no `.env`, so their `KUBECONFIG` is unpinned despite `USER.md` saying otherwise; diagnostics there must use GKE MCP tools with explicit resource paths.

args.title: RCA: Checkout pods failing to start after build update on gitops-pilot-20260916-132249
args.body:
Production incident, on-call engaged.

Cluster: gitops-pilot-20260916-132249 (project fuxiaogao-gkedemos).

Symptom: the "checkout" workload has been running at only part of its usual replica count since a build update deployed this morning. New instances keep failing to start.

Do read-only diagnostics and return a grounded RCA:
- Current vs desired replicas for checkout; which pods are not Ready and why.
- Pod status/describe/events/logs for the failing pods (crash loop, OOMKill, image pull, probe failure, unschedulable, mount/secret/config error, quota).
- Whether the cause is the new image/config from this morning's update, or capacity/scheduling.
- Node and resource pressure, and any relevant HPA/autoscaler behavior.

Deliverable: root cause + a concrete proposed manifest patch (exact fields/values) suitable for a GitOps PR. Do not mutate cluster state.
